subject.title: [Feature Request] Add config encryption for credentials at rest

question: Should OpenClaw implement native encrypted-at-rest credential storage for current SQLite auth profiles and config-secret surfaces, and what key-management/recovery model should own it?
rationale: The remaining work decides credential custody, migration semantics, service startup, recovery, OAuth/rotating-token handling, and whether core owns encryption or continues to rely on SecretRefs and external secret stores.

options.title: Redesign Core Encryption Boundary
options.body: Implement a secops-owned design against the current SQLite/auth/config/doctor boundary with keychain or master-password custody, migration tests, recovery behavior, and audit proof.

options.title: Keep SecretRefs As The Boundary
options.body: Treat external secret managers plus audit/apply scrubbing as the supported posture and close or narrow native encryption requests after documenting the tradeoff.

options.title: Narrow To Diagnostics First
options.body: Ship stronger audit, doctor, and setup warnings for plaintext credentials while deferring native encryption until key custody is settled.

recommendation.title: Redesign Core Encryption Boundary
recommendation.body: Implement a secops-owned design against the current SQLite/auth/config/doctor boundary with keychain or master-password custody, migration tests, recovery behavior, and audit proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the closest prior auth-store sealing attempt and is listed for Agents and Security, making him the best routing candidate for the security-boundary decision.
